Google just separated the agent from the model.

At Gemini at Work, Google introduced the Gemini agent — a persistent enterprise agent that operates across work surfaces and selects among multiple underlying models. The key architectural decision: your workflows and enterprise context stay stable even when the model underneath changes.

This sounds technical. The business impact is anything but.

Until this week, choosing an enterprise AI vendor meant coupling your entire operation to one model. Your prompts, your data flows, your institutional knowledge — all tied to a single provider. Switching costs were enormous by design.

Google just deliberately broke that pattern. And Atlassian reinforced it the same week by launching AMP — giving AI agents their own identity and scoped authority inside team workflows.

The signal is unmistakable. The agent layer is becoming the durable enterprise asset. The model underneath is becoming interchangeable compute.

For any executive making AI platform decisions right now, this changes the evaluation criteria entirely. The right question is no longer which model leads today. It is which agent infrastructure will let you swap models without rebuilding everything.
